title: Improve Three.js performance, validated against Janus Studio
objective: Deliver engine performance improvements in the separate Three.js fork with reproducible before/after Janus Studio measurements and unchanged rendering/interaction correctness.

baseline.comparisonRule: Treat Janus current r183.2 compatibility, upstream r187 upgrade, and fork changes as three separate variants. Attribute fork gains only against source-equivalent upstream r187.
baseline.applicationSnapshot: Record current application source/fixture hashes, including relevant dirty files; require identical hashes for both members of every paired run.
baseline.integration: Use a local build/import alias and isolated cache/output directories. Keep one Three.js module identity across core, addons and any worker or dependent renderer imports. Preserve application source, package manifest and lockfile.

milestones.deliverable: Runnable engine and Janus Studio harness; representative scenes, backend identity, correctness controls and paired baseline evidence.
Rank CPU, upload, allocation, startup and picking costs; choose audited engine changes actually exercised by Janus.
Small independent fork commits with meaningful regression tests and equivalent output.
Repeated baseline/candidate engine and product runs, compatibility checks, regression budgets and retained-resource checks.
Published sanitized before/after report, commands, environment, source hashes, raw metrics, confidence intervals and remaining limits.

workloads.purpose: Open an actual Studio workspace and reach a nonempty interactive map; record loading/first-use latency. Use existing controlled fixtures without weakening product authentication.
Deterministic pan, zoom, orbit/tilt and settle sequence; retain expected visible detail and stable entity identities.
Repeated picks and sparse selection/style/geometry edits with correct visible changes and interaction results.
Load/unload or replace scene resources, repeated mount/dispose, and retained building/context meshes.
Exercise primary/comparison views with the same source snapshot and explicit cameras.
Use deterministic synthetic scene sizes selected after profiling; report counts/visible counts and mark reduced renderer fixtures separately from full Studio runs.

measurementProtocol.order: Alternate AB/BA or rotate baseline/candidate order; isolate CPU-heavy builds from timing runs.
measurementProtocol.inputControl: Same browser/version, actual backend/device, viewport, DPR, app hash, scene/seed, camera script and cache policy within each pair; publish warm/cold results separately.
measurementProtocol.backendControl: Qualify the WebGL2 path used by Janus first. Record actual backend and GPU identity; report fallback/software separately. Do not label a fallback as native WebGPU.
platforms: Mobile viewport and CPU-throttled Chrome as emulation, explicitly not physical mobile qualification
Firefox/WebKit compatibility where the application supports the tested path
metrics: frame-interval p50/p95/p99, separately from CPU render time
draw calls, visible geometry and program/pipeline counts
allocation/copy volume and retained resource counts/bytes where measurable
GPU completion time only when measured with a supported reliable method
measurementProtocol.statistics: Report per-round and paired distributions; bootstrap a 95% confidence interval of paired ratios. Do not treat every frame as an independent run.
measurementProtocol.instrumentation: Separate detailed tracing/counting from minimally instrumented timing; apply identical instrumentation to both variants. Unsupported measurements remain null with a reason.

primaryTarget.metric: p95 main-thread render/prepare CPU in at least one representative, profile-verified Janus Studio workload
primaryTarget.confidence: Paired improvement interval excludes zero; retain raw per-round results. This is a target, not an achieved result.

secondaryTargets: Reduce the profiled dominant upload/call/allocation cost by at least 50% when that is the selected optimization.
Reduce startup/picking latency by at least 10% if those paths are optimized.

regressionBudget.rule: No reproducible regression beyond the larger of 5% or 0.3ms in other timed render workloads. Report uncertain/noisy outcomes as unqualified; do not infer success from one run.

correctness: Existing Studio and retained-building browser assertions pass for the supported candidate path.
Nonempty visible geometry, stable entities, picks, selections, edit results and comparison views match the control.
Identical framebuffer hashes for deterministic unchanged-rendering engine cases; any necessary tolerance is defined and justified before the candidate run.
No new JavaScript, GL, validation or context-loss errors. No missing detail or skipped useful work counted as a speedup.
acceptance.lifetime: No monotonic growth of live renderer resources/listeners after repeated teardown; investigate heap/GPU-byte changes independently from object counts.
engineChecks: Focused regressions for every changed code path.
Core/addon unit suites and relevant lint/build gates.
Document pre-existing failures separately; do not remove numerical assertions or silently skip unsupported backends.
acceptance.completion: At least one useful engine change meets the primary target and correctness/regression gates against Janus Studio, with reproducible results and tested fork commits. Microbenchmark-only gains cannot complete the goal.

boundaries: Engine changes belong in this fork. Do not redesign or optimize the map adapter to claim a Three.js gain.
Profile before selecting candidates; park audit items unused by Janus instead of claiming application benefit.
Keep unrelated Atlas work intact. Do not alter backend admission, source selection, tenant/authentication or deployment state.
Use synthetic or explicitly authorized local benchmark data. Keep private application source, credentials and customer data out of the public fork. Publish sanitized metrics only.
No deployment, upstream PR, or dependency rollout is implied by local benchmark qualification.

currentProgress.candidateFeature: Opt-in bounded inactive WebGL program cache, maxInactivePrograms; default zero.

engineQualification.releaseBuild: 5 outputs compile without warnings; checked-in builds unchanged

currentProgress.baselineSetupIssue: Pre-existing governed binding key exceeds style parser 512-character limit; upstream r187 cannot reach a nonempty governed frame. Kept separate from supported synthetic Studio workload.
currentProgress.fullStudioBaselineScope: Actual Studio UI and native renderer, with 400 deterministic synthetic unadmitted parcels through the normal runtime layer API. Governed presentation path is not qualified.

retained3dPairedBenchmark.scope: Actual native/illustration renderer fixture, not full Studio UI

rendererLifetime.wholePageHeap: unqualified: baseline and fork growth remains

scaling100PairedBenchmark.scope: Full Studio UI, 100 synthetic unadmitted parcels
scaling100PairedBenchmark.recovery: Entire pair 5 replaced after unmeasured browser startup failure; no selection by timing.

mobileEmulationPairedBenchmark.scope: 390x844 Chrome viewport, 4x CPU throttling, not physical mobile

currentProgress.finalChecks: Fresh full Chrome core/addons, Firefox/WebKit focused cache, core/test lint and five-output warning-free release build pass after bulk-disposal followup.
remainingLimits: Governed presentation blocked by upstream binding-key parser limit; full UI uses explicitly synthetic unadmitted data.
Whole-page retained heap and all-page listeners grow in both variants; renderer-owned GL handles/subscriptions retire to zero.
GPU completion/residency and allocation bytes unmeasured; startup/pick/edit latency remains diagnostic.
One Apple M1 Pro host; mobile is emulation. Cache is opt-in16/default0; no rollout or deployment.
